templates.name: Editorial Shoot
templates.label: New template
templates.object: 35mm film canister with the film leader pulled out
templates.alt: A teal chrome 35mm film canister with amber film pulled from its side
templates.preview: From first idea to call sheet: vision, references, casting, shot plan and the day itself.

about: From first idea to call sheet: vision, references, casting, shot plan and the day itself.

Made for Creative Director, Photographer and Stylist roles. It runs the pre-production of a fashion or editorial shoot as eleven steps across four stages: Blueprint, Pre-production, Shoot and Safeguards.
Work through it as a map or a list. Each step builds on the ones before it, and the call sheet compiles itself from your shot plan and team.
howTo: Open the template and name the project: Nia sets up the workspace.
Start with Vision, then build the Concept Blueprint and Mood References.
Cast, style, scout and assemble the team in Pre-production.
Plan every shot in Shot Planning: order, location, cast, setup and running time.
Open Callsheet Distribution: the day compiles from the shot plan and team. Export it as a PDF.
Finish with Contingency and Gear Inventory before the shoot.

faq.a: From first idea to call sheet: vision, references, casting, shot plan and the day itself.
Mainly Creative Director, Photographer and Stylist. It sits in Workflows and is used mainly in pre-production.

faq.q: How is it different from Call Sheet?
faq.a: Editorial Shoot covers from first idea to call sheet. Call Sheet covers the daily blueprint for a shoot, sent to cast and crew the night before. Many teams use both.

faq.q: Does it connect to my other documents?
faq.a: It lives in your project next to related templates like Call Sheet and Shotlist, so the whole job stays in one place.
Yes. Download it as a PDF to send or print.
